items.source_en:
Established permanent position in the valley. Natural shelter from the cliff face, fresh water from runoff. 

The crashed LAAT gave us enough salvage to rig irrigation -- stripped the fuel cells for power, hull plating for greenhouse frames.

First harvest: Saleucami grain, tubers, whatever seeds we could scavenge from abandoned homesteads. The soil's better than I expected. The war left a lot of farmland empty.

A farmer came through last week. Bartered engine parts for food. Didn't ask questions. That'll work.

The others want to take down the memorial markers -- say they draw attention. But if we forget who we buried, what's the point of surviving?
items.legacy_ko:
계곡에 영구적인 거점을 마련했다. 절벽이 자연적인 은신처가 되어주고, 유출수로 신선한 물도 얻을 수 있다.

추락한 LAAT에서 얻은 고철로 관개 시설을 만들었다. 연료 셀은 동력원으로, 선체 장갑판은 온실 프레임으로 썼다.

첫 수확물: 살루카미 곡물, 덩이줄기, 버려진 농가에서 긁어모은 씨앗들. 토양은 생각보다 좋다. 전쟁 때문에 버려진 농지가 많다.

지난주에 농부 한 명이 지나갔다. 엔진 부품을 식량과 교환했다. 아무것도 묻지 않았다. 괜찮은 거래였다.

다른 사람들은 추모비를 철거하고 싶어 한다. 눈에 띈다는 이유에서다. 하지만 우리가 누구를 묻었는지 잊어버린다면, 살아남는 게 무슨 의미가 있겠나?

items.source_en:
I've been working the spacelanes for years, and I've survived this long by having a strict set of rules. 

The biggest being, never take a job if you don't know the risks. That's like betting your last cred on a gut-shot straight draw. And yet here I am, doing just that. It's a sick way to go out, but those are the terms.

Our cred flow had just about run dry when I got word of a big score from one of my old gang contacts. We meet the client at Euphorika. He doesn't give me a name, or any of the usual small talk. Fine, I hate small talk. He just wants to know the class of my ship, and the size of my cargo hold. I give him the data, and I tell him if it's not enough, we'll make room.

Satisfied, the client tells me he wants me to pick up a package in the Moloch system, and deliver it to Rasapan II. He hands me the coordinates for both the pick up and the drop on a piece of paper. Doesn't give any other details. Just removes himself from the scene. 

I tell my first mate about the job, and he tells me to turn it down. Things get heated, and I have to pull rank. But he's right about one thing. Something about this job doesn't feel right. Like you're holding pocket kings and you just know the big blind has Aces. But at this point, it's the only play.
items.legacy_ko:
수년간 우주 항로를 누비며 살아남은 비결은 엄격한 규칙을 지키는 것이었다.

가장 중요한 건, 위험을 모르는 일은 절대 맡지 않는다는 것이다. 그건 마지막 크레딧을 걸고 승산 없는 도박을 하는 것과 같으니까. 그런데 지금 내가 바로 그 짓을 하고 있다. 끝이 뻔히 보이는 어리석은 짓이지만, 그게 조건이었다.

크레딧이 바닥날 때쯤 옛 조직 인맥으로부터 큰 건이 있다는 소식을 들었다. 유포리카에서 의뢰인을 만났다. 그는 이름도 밝히지 않았고, 흔한 잡담도 없었다. 좋다, 난 잡담은 질색이니까. 그는 그저 내 함선의 등급과 화물칸 크기만 물었다. 데이터를 넘겨주며 부족하면 공간을 만들겠다고 했다.

만족한 의뢰인은 몰로크 성계에서 화물을 픽업해 라사판 II로 배달하라고 했다. 그는 픽업과 하차 좌표가 적힌 종이 한 장을 건네고는 아무런 설명도 없이 사라졌다.

locations.vanilla_source_en:
I've been working the spacelanes for years, and I've survived this long by having a strict set of rules. 

The biggest being, never take a job if you don't know the risks. That's like betting your last cred on a gut-shot straight draw. And yet here I am, doing just that. It's a sick way to go out, but those are the terms.

Our cred flow had just about run dry when I got word of a big score from one of my old gang contacts. We meet the client at Euphorika. He doesn't give me a name, or any of the usual small talk. Fine, I hate small talk. He just wants to know the class of my ship, and the size of my cargo hold. I give him the data, and I tell him if it's not enough, we'll make room.

Satisfied, the client tells me he wants me to pick up a package in the Moloch system, and deliver it to Vectera. He hands me the coordinates for both the pick up and the drop on a piece of paper. Doesn't give any other details. Just removes himself from the scene. 

I tell my first mate about the job, and he tells me to turn it down. Things get heated, and I have to pull rank. But he's right about one thing. Something about this job doesn't feel right. Like you're holding pocket kings and you just know the big blind has Aces. But at this point, it's the only play.
